'''Hamidou Touré''' (born 14 October 1954) is a [[Burkina Faso|Burkinabès]] mathematician who has played a significant role in the development of mathematics programs in Burkina Faso, from the pre-school level to university level.

== Life and career ==

=== Early life and education ===
Hamidou Touré was born on 14 October 1954.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Hamidou Touré - Mathematician of the African Diaspora |url=http://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/PEEPS2/toure_hamidou.html |access-date=2023-04-07 |website=www.math.buffalo.edu |archive-date=2023-04-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230407181749/http://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/PEEPS2/toure_hamidou.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He has earned several degrees in mathematics, including a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in 1982 and a unique doctorate in 1994 from the [[University of Franche-Comté]] in Besançon, France, and a doctorate d'état in 1995 from the [[University of Ouagadougou|Université de Ouagadougou]] in Burkina Faso.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Citation |last=Johnson |first=David P. |chapter=Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso |date=2005-04-07 |chapter-url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1093/acref/9780195301731.013.42825 |title=African American Studies Center |access-date=2023-04-07 |publisher=Oxford University Press |doi=10.1093/acref/9780195301731.013.42825 |isbn=978-0-19-530173-1 |archive-date=2023-04-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230413170443/https://oxfordaasc.com/display/10.1093/acref/9780195301731.001.0001/acref-9780195301731-e-42825;jsessionid=024F84CC11D6904F9ACAC7DD63E1EB69 |url-status=live |chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref>

=== Career ===
Toure joined the Mathematics Department of the University of Ouagadougou in Burkina Faso. He gradually climbed the academic ranks and was eventually appointed as a full professor in 2002.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Toure Hamidou {{!}} The AAS |url=https://www.aasciences.africa/fellow/toure-hamidou |access-date=2023-04-07 |website=www.aasciences.africa |archive-date=2023-04-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230407181749/https://www.aasciences.africa/fellow/toure-hamidou |url-status=live }}</ref>

He has held various positions of leadership at the Institute of Mathematics and Physics, including being the Head of the Mathematics Department, Head of the Postgraduate Programs, Deputy Director of the Center of Computer Sciences in Charge of Distance Learning and ICT, Director of the [[University of Pedagogical Sciences]] Center, Director of the [[African Virtual University]], Director of the Distance Learning Degree of Multimedia Communicator, Director of the Laboratory of LAME Equations and Mathematical Analysis,<ref>{{Cite web |title=University of Ouagadougou, Mathematical Analysis of Equations Laboratory (LAME), UFR |url=https://digital.library.txstate.edu/concept/0e9865cc-2951-47f7-987d-8df18b8ecf04 |access-date=2023-04-07 |website=digital.library.txstate.edu |archive-date=2023-04-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230407183415/https://digital.library.txstate.edu/concept/0e9865cc-2951-47f7-987d-8df18b8ecf04 |url-status=live }}</ref> and Director of [[African Mathematics Millennium Science Initiative]] (AMMSI)'s West African Regional Office.<ref name=":1" />

In addition to his academic positions, he has also served as a Senior Associate at the ICTP in Trieste, Italy, and was a Co-Founder and Coordinator of the Research Network PDE Modelling and Control. He is a member of the Executive Committee of the [[African Mathematical Union]] (UMA) and various other professional societies.<ref name=":1" />

Toure's involvement in mathematics goes beyond research and teaching. He has played a significant role in the development of mathematics programs in Burkina Faso, from the pre-school level to university level.<ref>{{Cite arXiv |last=Gouba |first=Laure |date=2016-08-11 |title=African Doctorates in Mathematics from Burkina-Faso |class=math.HO |eprint=1608.03508 }}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Pr Hamidou Touré : Des hommages à l'infini pour un enseignant de mathématiques - leFaso.net |url=https://lefaso.net/spip.php?article86266 |access-date=2023-04-07 |website=lefaso.net |language=fr |archive-date=2023-04-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230407182420/https://lefaso.net/spip.php?article86266 |url-status=live }}</ref> In addition, he is a member of the African Mathematical Union, and he has participated in the organisation of the African Mathematical Schools.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Hamidou Toure {{!}} CIMPA |url=https://www.cimpa.info/node/5733 |access-date=2023-04-07 |website=www.cimpa.info |archive-date=2023-04-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230407181751/https://www.cimpa.info/node/5733 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Toure has been a member of the International Centre for Pure and Applied Mathematics (CIMPA), and he has attended conferences and given lectures in various countries, including Japan, India, and France.<ref name=":2" /> He is also a permanent secretary of the [[National Academy of Sciences of Burkina Faso]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Partnership (IAP) |first=the InterAcademy |title=Hamidou Toure |url=https://www.interacademies.org/person/hamidou-toure |access-date=2023-04-07 |website=www.interacademies.org |language=en-GB |archive-date=2023-04-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230407183251/https://www.interacademies.org/person/hamidou-toure |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Research ==
{{Scholia}}
Toure has published research on partial differential equations, nonlinear semigroups, and mathematical modeling, among other topics.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Hamidou Touré - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=89671 |access-date=2023-04-07 |website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu |archive-date=2023-04-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230407181748/https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=89671 |url-status=live }}</ref> Toure has made significant contributions to the field of mathematics. He is primarily focused on the study of nonlinear elliptic parabolic equations within the context of evolution equations in [[Banach space]]s.<ref>{{Cite book == Awards and honours ==
Touré is the recipient of the [[International Mathematical Union]] (IMU) Breakthrough Prize, awarded for his contributions to the development of mathematics in Burkina Faso and Africa as a whole.<ref name=":4" /> He is also a Fellow of the [[African Academy of Sciences]] since 2009.<ref name=":1" />
